<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Package #</span>



This package provides an easy and modular way to build and train simple or complex neural networks using \[Torch](https://github.com/torch/torch7/blob/master/README.md):

&#x20;\* Modules are the bricks used to build neural networks. Each are themselves neural networks, but can be combined with other networks using containers to create complex neural networks:

&#x20;  \* \[Module](doc/module.md#nn.Module): abstract class inherited by all modules;

&#x20;  \* \[Containers](doc/containers.md#nn.Containers): composite and decorator classes like \[`Sequential`](doc/containers.md#nn.Sequential), \[`Parallel`](doc/containers.md#nn.Parallel), \[`Concat`](doc/containers.md#nn.Concat) and \[`NaN`](doc/containers.md#nn.NaN);

&#x20;  \* \[Transfer <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>](doc/transfer.md#nn.transfer.dok): non-linear <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span> like \[`Tanh`](doc/transfer.md#nn.Tanh) and \[`Sigmoid`](doc/transfer.md#nn.Sigmoid);

&#x20;  \* \[Simple layers](doc/simple.md#nn.simplelayers.dok): like \[`Linear`](doc/simple.md#nn.Linear), \[`Mean`](doc/simple.md#nn.Mean), \[`Max`](doc/simple.md#nn.Max) and \[`Reshape`](doc/simple.md#nn.Reshape);

&#x20;  \* \[Table layers](doc/table.md#nn.TableLayers): layers <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> manipulating `table`s like \[`SplitTable`](doc/table.md#nn.SplitTable), \[`ConcatTable`](doc/table.md#nn.ConcatTable) and \[`JoinTable`](doc/table.md#nn.JoinTable);

&#x20;  \* \[Convolution layers](doc/convolution.md#nn.convlayers.dok): \[`Temporal`](doc/convolution.md#nn.TemporalModules),  \[`Spatial`](doc/convolution.md#nn.SpatialModules) and \[`Volumetric`](doc/convolution.md#nn.VolumetricModules) convolutions;

&#x20;\* Criterions compute a gradient according to a given loss <span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> given an input and a target:

&#x20;  \* \[Criterions](doc/criterion.md#nn.Criterions): a list of all criterions, including \[`Criterion`](doc/criterion.md#nn.Criterion), the abstract class;

&#x20;  \* \[`MSECriterion`](doc/criterion.md#nn.MSECriterion): the Mean Squared Error criterion used <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> regression;

&#x20;  \* \[`ClassNLLCriterion`](doc/criterion.md#nn.ClassNLLCriterion): the Negative Log Likelihood criterion used <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> classification;

&#x20;\* Additional documentation:

&#x20;  \* \[Overview](doc/overview.md#nn.overview.dok) of the package essentials including modules, containers and training;

&#x20;  \* \[Training](doc/training.md#nn.traningneuralnet.dok): how to train a neural network using \[`StochasticGradient`](doc/training.md#nn.StochasticGradient);

&#x20;  \* \[Testing](doc/testing.md): how to <span class="hljs-built\_in">test</span> your modules.

&#x20;  \* \[Experimental Modules](https://github.com/clementfarabet/lua---nnx/blob/master/README.md): a package containing experimental modules and criteria.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Continuous Integration \&amp; Testing ##</span>



Every implementation <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> this repository is exercised by \[GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/ci.yml). To run the suites locally:



| Implementation | Unit tests | E2E demos |

|---|---|---|

| a9nn (pure Lua) | `<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> lang/a9nn \&amp;\&amp; lua run\_tests.lua` | `lua examples/\&lt;example\&gt;.lua` |

| Prolog | `<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> lang/pl \&amp;\&amp; swipl -q -l test\_nn.pl -g run\_tests -t halt` (also `test\_modules.pl` / `run\_module\_tests`, `test\_nd.pl` / `run\_nd\_tests`, `test\_consistency.pl` / `run\_consistency\_tests`) | `swipl -q -l demo.pl -g run\_all\_demos -t halt` |

| P-Lingua | `bash lang/pli/validate.sh` | — |

| Raku | `<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> lang/raku \&amp;\&amp; raku test-nn.raku` | `raku demo.raku`, `raku example.raku` |

| Racket | `<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> lang/rkt \&amp;\&amp; racket test-nn.rkt` | `racket demo.rkt`, `racket example.rkt` |

| Scheme (Guile) | `<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> lang/scm \&amp;\&amp; guile --no-auto-compile -l nn.scm -l test-nn.scm -c <span class="hljs-string">'(run-all-tests)'</span>` | `guile --no-auto-compile -l nn.scm -l demo.scm -c <span class="hljs-string">'(run-all-demos)'</span>` |

| Isabelle/HOL | `isabelle build -d lang/isa -v NN` (the build re-runs every proof and every `<span class="hljs-built\_in">eval</span>`-based <span class="hljs-built\_in">test</span>) | Demos and examples run as part of the same build |

| THNN (C backend) | `bash lang/c/THNN/check.sh` (structural smoke check) | — |

| Torch/nn (Lua) | Requires a full \[Torch7](https://github.com/torch/distro) install: `luarocks make rocks/nn-scm-1.rockspec` <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> `lua -lnn -e <span class="hljs-string">"nn.test()"</span>` (CI performs a syntax check of all modules; the opt-in nightly `torch-legacy` job attempts the full build) | — |



Lint Lua sources with `luacheck lang/lua lang/a9nn` and build the docs with `mkdocs build --strict`.



<span class="hljs-comment">### Cross-implementation consistency</span>



All seven ports agree numerically on a single deterministic fixture,

\[`docs/fixtures/xor\_fixture.json`](docs/fixtures/xor\_fixture.json): a fixed

2-2-1 sigmoid MLP with known weights, an input, and the expected forward output

and MSE loss. Each port constructs the network and asserts the results to a

tolerance (10⁻⁶ <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> the <span class="hljs-built\_in">float</span> ports; 10⁻³ <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> Isabelle<span class="hljs-string">'s exact-rational

approximation layer, in `lang/isa/NN\_Consistency.thy`). A disagreement between

any two ports fails CI, so the implementations cannot silently drift apart.



\### CI jobs



The `ci-success` job is a single fan-in gate suitable as a required status

check. Per-language jobs run only when their `lang/\&lt;x\&gt;/` subtree changes (or on

the default branch / manual dispatch). The `torch-legacy` job runs the full

legacy Torch7 `nn.test()` suite on a nightly schedule and manual dispatch only,

and is best-effort (`continue-on-error`).

<span class="hljs-comment"># Implementation Summary: Extended Pure Prolog Neural Network (nn.pl)</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">## Overview</span>

Successfully extended the Pure Prolog neural network implementation with a comprehensive modular architecture inspired by Torch/nn, adding containers, multiple activation <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>, loss criterions, and simple layer modules <span class="hljs-keyword">while</span> maintaining full backward compatibility.



<span class="hljs-comment">## What Was Implemented</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### 1. Container Modules</span>

Containers allow composition of neural network components:



\- \*\*Sequential\*\*: Chains modules together <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> feed-forward fashion

&#x20; - Example: `sequential(\[Linear1, Tanh, Linear2, LogSoftMax])`

&#x20; - Forward pass automatically flows through all modules <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> order



\- \*\*Concat\*\*: Applies multiple modules to same input and concatenates outputs

&#x20; - Example: `concat(1, \[Branch1, Branch2])`

&#x20; - Useful <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> parallel processing paths



<span class="hljs-comment">### 2. Activation/Transfer Modules</span>

Standardized activation <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span> as modules:



\- \*\*Sigmoid\*\*: Logistic sigmoid <span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> (0 to 1 range)

\- \*\*Tanh\*\*: Hyperbolic tangent (-1 to 1 range)

\- \*\*ReLU\*\*: Rectified Linear Unit (max(0, x))

\- \*\*SoftMax\*\*: Converts logits to probabilities (sums to 1)

\- \*\*LogSoftMax\*\*: Log of SoftMax (numerically stable <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> classification)



All can be used via `module\_forward/3` <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> consistent interface.



<span class="hljs-comment">### 3. Criterion/Loss Modules</span>

Multiple loss <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> different tasks:



\- \*\*MSECriterion\*\*: Mean Squared Error <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> regression

\- \*\*ClassNLLCriterion\*\*: Negative Log Likelihood <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> multi-class classification

&#x20; - Use with LogSoftMax output

\- \*\*BCECriterion\*\*: Binary Cross Entropy <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> binary classification

\- \*\*AbsCriterion\*\*: L1/Absolute Error loss



All support both forward (loss computation) and backward (gradient computation).



<span class="hljs-comment">### 4. Simple Layer Modules</span>

Building blocks <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> network construction:



\- \*\*Linear\*\*: Fully connected linear transformation (y = Wx + b)

\- \*\*Identity\*\*: Pass-through layer (useful <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> containers)

\- \*\*Reshape\*\*: Reshape tensor dimensions

\- \*\*Mean\*\*: Reduction by mean along dimension

\- \*\*Max\*\*: Reduction by max along dimension



<span class="hljs-comment">## Files Created/Modified</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### New Files:</span>

1\. \*\*test\_modules.pl\*\* (276 lines)

&#x20;  - 16 individual module tests

&#x20;  - 1 integration <span class="hljs-built\_in">test</span>

&#x20;  - Tests all new functionality

&#x20;  - All tests pass ✓



2\. \*\*demo\_modules.pl\*\* (287 lines)

&#x20;  - 7 comprehensive demonstrations

<span class="hljs-comment"># a9nn — Lua Neural Network Framework with Cognitive Agent Architecture</span>



\*\*a9nn\*\* is a self-contained Lua neural network framework that extends the

classic `torch/nn` API with a full \*\*cognitive agent architecture\*\*:

Echo State Reservoir Networks, OpenCog AtomSpace, personality-driven

multi-agent systems, and parallel LLaMA.cpp orchestration.



It runs without Torch (pure Lua 5.1+) and automatically upgrades to Torch

tensors when Torch is present.



\---



<span class="hljs-comment">## Quick Start</span>



```lua

\-- From the repo root:

package.path = <span class="hljs-string">"lang/a9nn/?.lua;"</span> .. package.path



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> nn = require(<span class="hljs-string">'a9nn'</span>)



\-- ── Classic MLP ───────────────────────────────────────────────

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> mlp = nn.Sequential()

mlp:add(nn.Linear(2, 8))

mlp:add(nn.Tanh())

mlp:add(nn.Linear(8, 1))



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> criterion = nn.MSECriterion()

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> x = nn.Tensor.new({0.5, -0.3})

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> y = nn.Tensor.new({1.0})

mlp:forward(x)

mlp:backward(x, criterion:backward(mlp.output, y))

mlp:updateParameters(0.01)



\-- ── Full NNECCO cognitive agent ───────────────────────────────

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> agent = nn.NNECCOAgent({

&#x20;  stateSize      = 64,

&#x20;  reservoirSize  = 847,

&#x20;  llamaInstances = 4,    -- 4 parallel LLaMA.cpp instances

&#x20;  stubMode       = <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>, -- <span class="hljs-built\_in">set</span> <span class="hljs-literal">false</span> when llama.cpp servers are running

})



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> result = agent:process(<span class="hljs-string">"Explain gradient descent"</span>)

<span class="hljs-built\_in">print</span>(result.output.text)

<span class="hljs-built\_in">print</span>(<span class="hljs-string">"Action:"</span>, result.action, <span class="hljs-string">"Layer:"</span>, result.layer)

```



\---



<span class="hljs-comment">## Architecture</span>



```

nn.Module

├── Standard NN Modules

│   ├── nn.Linear            Fully-connected layer

│   ├── nn.Sequential        Feed-forward container

│   ├── nn.Tanh / Sigmoid    Activation <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>

│   ├── nn.ReLU / LeakyReLU  Rectified activations

│   ├── nn.ELU               Exponential linear unit

│   ├── nn.SoftMax           Probability normalisation

│   └── nn.LogSoftMax        Log-probability normalisation

│

├── Criterions

│   ├── nn.MSECriterion           Mean squared error

│   ├── nn.BCECriterion           Binary cross-entropy

│   ├── nn.ClassNLLCriterion      Negative log-likelihood

│   ├── nn.CrossEntropyCriterion  Softmax + NLL combined

│   └── nn.SmoothL1Criterion      Huber / smooth-L1

│

├── Cognitive Modules

│   ├── nn.EchoReservoir     Echo State Network reservoir

│   ├── nn.AtomSpace         OpenCog hypergraph knowledge base

│   ├── nn.Personality       Mutable personality trait tensor

│   ├── nn.EpisodicMemory    Priority-weighted experience replay

│   └── nn.LLaMAOrchestrator 1-9 parallel LLaMA.cpp instances

│

└── Agents

&#x20;   ├── nn.Agent             Base RL agent (DQN-style)

&#x20;   ├── nn.CognitiveAgent    Multi-agent orchestrator with delegation

&#x20;   └── nn.NNECCOAgent       Full NNECCO pipeline (12-step EchoBeats)

```

<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Implementation in PLingua</span>



A comprehensive P-Systems membrane computing implementation of feedforward neural networks with backpropagation training and modular architecture.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Overview</span>



This implementation demonstrates how neural network algorithms can be expressed using P-Systems and membrane computing principles. It provides a complete neural network library written <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> PLingua, the programming language <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> P-Systems.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Features</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Core Functionality</span>

\- \*\*Feedforward Neural Networks\*\*: Arbitrary layer sizes and architectures

\- \*\*Backpropagation\*\*: Complete training algorithm with gradient descent

\- \*\*Multiple Activation Functions\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU

\- \*\*Softmax\*\*: For multi-class classification with probability distributions

\- \*\*Loss Functions\*\*: MSE (regression), NLL (classification), BCE (binary), Absolute Error

\- \*\*Modular Architecture\*\*: Composable neural network components



<span class="hljs-comment">### P-Systems Implementation</span>

\- \*\*Membrane-Based Neurons\*\*: Each neuron is a computational membrane

\- \*\*Rule-Based Computation\*\*: Forward/backward passes implemented as evolution rules

\- \*\*Inter-Membrane Communication\*\*: Data flows between layers via communication rules

\- \*\*Weight Evolution\*\*: Training updates weights through rule application

\- \*\*Parallel Processing\*\*: P-Systems natural parallelism models concurrent neural computation



<span class="hljs-comment">### Modular Components</span>

\- \*\*Container Modules\*\*: Sequential, Concat, Parallel, ConcatTable, table ops (CAdd/CSub/CMul/CMax/CMin), Identity, Reshape

\- \*\*Transfer Modules\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LeakyReLU, PReLU, ELU, SELU, GELU, Softplus, HardTanh, HardSigmoid, LogSigmoid, LogSoftMax

\- \*\*Layer Modules\*\*: Linear/Dense, LookupTable (embedding), Bilinear, SparseLinear

\- \*\*Criterion Modules\*\*: MSE, NLL, BCE, Absolute Error, CrossEntropy, SmoothL1/Huber, Margin, KLDiv, weighted NLL

\- \*\*Initialization\*\*: Xavier/Glorot and He/Kaiming schemes via `linear\_layer\_init`

\- \*\*Graph Neural Networks\*\*: Message passing, GCN, graph attention (GAT), graph readout — membranes as graph nodes

\- \*\*Neuroevolution\*\*: Genome membranes, mutation, crossover, division-based reproduction, tournament selection, NEAT-style topology evolution

\- \*\*Bayesian Layers\*\*: Weight distributions, reparameterization trick, KL regularization, Monte-Carlo uncertainty estimates

\- \*\*Transformer Decoder\*\*: Causal masking, masked self-attention, cross-attention, decoder stacks, positional encodings, greedy decoding



<span class="hljs-comment">## Installation</span>



No installation required! Simply ensure you have a PLingua simulator or interpreter.



<span class="hljs-comment">### Requirements</span>

\- PLingua 5.0+ (recommended)

\- P-Lingua Framework from \[https://github.com/RGNC/plingua](https://github.com/RGNC/plingua)

\- Java Runtime Environment (<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> P-Lingua simulator)



<span class="hljs-comment">### Getting PLingua</span>

```bash

<span class="hljs-comment"># Clone P-Lingua repository</span>

git <span class="hljs-built\_in">clone</span> https://github.com/RGNC/plingua.git

<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> plingua



<span class="hljs-comment"># Build (requires Java)</span>

ant jar



<span class="hljs-comment"># Or download pre-built from http://www.p-lingua.org</span>

```



<span class="hljs-comment">## Quick Start</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Basic Network Creation</span>



```plingua

/\* Create a simple feedforward network \*/

\[network

&#x20;   \[layer1 linear\_layer(2, 3)]<span class="hljs-string">'network

&#x20;   \[activation1 sigmoid\_activation]'</span>network

&#x20;   \[layer2 linear\_layer(3, 1)]<span class="hljs-string">'network

&#x20;   \[activation2 sigmoid\_activation]'</span>network

]<span class="hljs-string">'main



/\* Make prediction on input \[0.5, 0.8] \*/

\[input{1, 50}, input{2, 80}]'</span>network  /\* Values scaled by 100 \*/

```



<span class="hljs-comment">### Training a Network</span>



```plingua

/\* Define training data \*/

training\_data{

&#x20;   sample{\[0, 0], 0},

&#x20;   sample{\[0, 100], 100},

&#x20;   sample{\[100, 0], 100},

&#x20;   sample{\[100, 100], 0}

}



/\* Train XOR network \*/

train\_network(xor\_network, training\_data, 1000, 50)

```



<span class="hljs-comment">### Using Pre-built Architectures</span>



```plingua

/\* XOR network (classic <span class="hljs-built\_in">test</span>) \*/

xor\_network



/\* Binary classifier \*/

binary\_classifier(input\_size: 2, hidden\_size: 4)



/\* Multi-class classifier \*/

multiclass\_classifier(input\_size: 4, hidden\_size: 8, num\_classes: 3)

<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Implementation in Pure Isabelle/HOL</span>



A pure \[Isabelle/HOL](https://isabelle.in.tum.de) rendering of the neural

network library: the same feedforward networks, module system and

criterions as the sibling implementations, but as a \*definitional theory\*

whose invariants are machine-checked proofs rather than <span class="hljs-built\_in">test</span> assertions.



The library is derived from the Z++ formal specifications <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span>

\[`docs/`](../../docs) and mirrors the functional implementations <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span>

\[`lang/scm`](../scm), \[`lang/rkt`](../rkt) and \[`lang/raku`](../raku)

<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">function</span>.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Features</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Core functionality</span>

\- \*\*Feedforward neural networks\*\*: arbitrary layer sizes and architectures

\- \*\*Simplified backpropagation\*\*: activation caching, MSE gradient, SGD update

\- \*\*Activation <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LogSoftmax

\- \*\*Loss <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>\*\*: MSE, Classification NLL, Binary Cross Entropy, Absolute Error

\- \*\*Vector/matrix operations\*\*: dot product, matrix–vector product, transpose,

&#x20; element-wise arithmetic, reductions



<span class="hljs-comment">### Modular architecture</span>

\- \*\*Module system\*\*: a single `module` datatype (a \*deep embedding\*) with a

&#x20; primitive-recursive `module\_forward`

\- \*\*Container modules\*\*: `Sequential`, `Concat`

\- \*\*Transfer modules\*\*: `Sigmoid`, `Tanh`, `ReLU`, `Softmax`, `LogSoftmax`

\- \*\*Layer modules\*\*: `Linear`, `Identity`, `Reshape`, `Mean`, `Max`

\- \*\*Criterion modules\*\*: `MSECriterion`, `ClassNLLCriterion`, `BCECriterion`,

&#x20; `AbsCriterion`



<span class="hljs-comment">### What Isabelle adds</span>

\- \*\*Proved invariants\*\* instead of sampled assertions — see

&#x20; \[`NN\_Properties.thy`](NN\_Properties.thy)

\- \*\*Exact real arithmetic\*\* <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> the specification layer: `sigmoid`, `tanh`,

&#x20; `exp` and `<span class="hljs-built\_in">ln</span>` are the genuine mathematical <span class="hljs-built\_in">functions</span>, not floats

\- \*\*Derivative correctness\*\*: the activation derivatives used by training are

&#x20; proved to \*be\* the analytic derivatives (`has\_real\_derivative`)

\- \*\*Executable mirror\*\*: an approximation layer (`NN\_Exec.thy`) makes every

&#x20; definition runnable over exact rationals, so demos and regression tests

&#x20; execute inside the logic



<span class="hljs-comment">## Requirements</span>



\- Isabelle2025-2 (or any recent release); no Archive of Formal Proofs entries

&#x20; and no add-on components are required

\- The session builds on `HOL-Library`, <span class="hljs-built\_in">which</span> ships with the distribution



<span class="hljs-comment">### Installing Isabelle (CI / fresh machines)</span>



The official `isabelle.in.tum.de` download redirects to

`dist.isabelle.cit.tum.de`, <span class="hljs-built\_in">which</span> is not always reachable from CI. Prefer the

helper script, <span class="hljs-built\_in">which</span> tries durable HTTPS mirrors first, verifies the tarball

SHA-256, and unpacks into `\~/isabelle-dist`:



```bash

<span class="hljs-comment"># from the repository root</span>

bash lang/isa/install-isabelle.sh

<span class="hljs-built\_in">export</span> PATH=<span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$HOME</span>/isabelle-dist/bin:<span class="hljs-variable">$PATH</span>"</span>

```

\-----RAKU-----

<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Implementation in Raku</span>



A pure Raku implementation of feedforward neural networks with backpropagation training and modular architecture.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Features</span>



\- \*\*Feedforward Neural Networks\*\*: Build networks with arbitrary layer sizes

\- \*\*Multiple Activation Functions\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU with derivatives

\- \*\*Backpropagation Training\*\*: Complete gradient descent implementation

\- \*\*Modular Architecture\*\*: Compose networks using modules and containers

\- \*\*Loss Functions\*\*: MSE, Absolute Error, Binary Cross-Entropy

\- \*\*Vector/Matrix Operations\*\*: Comprehensive linear algebra utilities

\- \*\*Pure Raku\*\*: No external dependencies required



<span class="hljs-comment">## Installation</span>



This is a pure Raku implementation with no external dependencies. Simply ensure you have Raku installed:



```bash

<span class="hljs-comment"># Check if Raku is installed</span>

raku --version

```



If you need to install Raku, visit \[raku.org](https://raku.org/downloads/).



<span class="hljs-comment">## Quick Start</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Basic Neural Network</span>



```raku

use NN;



<span class="hljs-comment"># Create a network with 2 inputs, 4 hidden neurons, and 1 output</span>

my <span class="hljs-variable">$network</span> = create-network(\[2, 4, 1]);



<span class="hljs-comment"># Make a prediction</span>

my @output = predict(\[0.5, 0.8], <span class="hljs-variable">$network</span>);

say <span class="hljs-string">"Output: "</span>, @output;

```



<span class="hljs-comment">### Training a Network</span>



```raku

use NN;



<span class="hljs-comment"># Create training data for XOR problem</span>

my @training-data = \[

&#x20;   make-sample(\[0.0, 0.0], \[0.0]),

&#x20;   make-sample(\[0.0, 1.0], \[1.0]),

&#x20;   make-sample(\[1.0, 0.0], \[1.0]),

&#x20;   make-sample(\[1.0, 1.0], \[0.0])

];



<span class="hljs-comment"># Create and train network</span>

my <span class="hljs-variable">$network</span> = create-network(\[2, 4, 1]);

my <span class="hljs-variable">$trained</span> = train(@training-data, <span class="hljs-variable">$network</span>, 0.5, 1000);



<span class="hljs-comment"># Test predictions</span>

say <span class="hljs-string">"XOR(0, 0) = "</span>, predict(\[0.0, 0.0], <span class="hljs-variable">$trained</span>)\[0];

say <span class="hljs-string">"XOR(1, 1) = "</span>, predict(\[1.0, 1.0], <span class="hljs-variable">$trained</span>)\[0];

\-----RKT-----

<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Implementation in Pure Racket</span>



A comprehensive, pure Racket implementation of feedforward neural networks with backpropagation training and a modular architecture inspired by Torch/nn.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Features</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Core Functionality</span>

\- \*\*Feedforward Neural Networks\*\*: Arbitrary layer sizes and architectures

\- \*\*Backpropagation\*\*: Complete training algorithm with gradient descent

\- \*\*Multiple Activation Functions\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LogSoftmax

\- \*\*Loss Functions\*\*: MSE, Classification NLL, Binary Cross Entropy, Absolute Error

\- \*\*Vector/Matrix Operations\*\*: Dot product, matrix multiplication, element-wise operations



<span class="hljs-comment">### Modular Architecture</span>

\- \*\*Module System\*\*: Composable neural network components

\- \*\*Container Modules\*\*: Sequential, Concat <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> building complex networks

\- \*\*Transfer Modules\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LogSoftmax as modules

\- \*\*Layer Modules\*\*: Linear (fully connected), Identity, Reshape, Mean, Max

\- \*\*Criterion Modules\*\*: MSE, ClassNLL, BCE, Absolute Error



<span class="hljs-comment">### Pure Racket Implementation</span>

\- No external dependencies (uses `#lang racket`)

\- Clear, readable, and educational code

\- Idiomatic Racket style

\- Suitable <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> learning and prototyping



<span class="hljs-comment">## Installation</span>



No installation required! Simply use the Racket files <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> your project.



<span class="hljs-comment">### Requirements</span>

\- Racket 8.0+ (recommended)

\- Standard Racket distribution



<span class="hljs-comment">## Quick Start</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Basic Usage</span>



```racket

<span class="hljs-comment">#lang racket</span>

(require <span class="hljs-string">"nn.rkt"</span>)



; Create a network with layer sizes \[2, 3, 1]

(define net (create-network <span class="hljs-string">'(2 3 1)))



; Make a prediction

(define output (forward '</span>(0.5 0.8) net))

(displayln output)  ; =\&gt; (0.7123...)



; Train on data

<span class="hljs-comment"># Neural Network Implementation in Pure Scheme</span>



A comprehensive, pure Scheme implementation of feedforward neural networks with backpropagation training and a modular architecture inspired by Torch/nn.



<span class="hljs-comment">## Features</span>



<span class="hljs-comment">### Core Functionality</span>

\- \*\*Feedforward Neural Networks\*\*: Arbitrary layer sizes and architectures

\- \*\*Backpropagation\*\*: Complete training algorithm with gradient descent

\- \*\*Multiple Activation Functions\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LogSoftmax

\- \*\*Loss Functions\*\*: MSE, Classification NLL, Binary Cross Entropy, Absolute Error

\- \*\*Vector/Matrix Operations\*\*: Dot product, matrix multiplication, element-wise operations



<span class="hljs-comment">### Modular Architecture</span>

\- \*\*Module System\*\*: Composable neural network components

\- \*\*Container Modules\*\*: Sequential, Concat <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> building complex networks

\- \*\*Transfer Modules\*\*: Sigmoid, Tanh, ReLU, Softmax, LogSoftmax as modules

\- \*\*Layer Modules\*\*: Linear (fully connected), Identity, Reshape, Mean, Max

\- \*\*Criterion Modules\*\*: MSE, ClassNLL, BCE, Absolute Error



<span class="hljs-comment">### Pure Scheme Implementation</span>

\- No external dependencies

\- Designed <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> GNU Guile (recommended)

\- May require minor adjustments <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> other Scheme implementations (see Compatibility section)

\- Clear, readable, and educational code

\- Suitable <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> learning and prototyping



<span class="hljs-comment">## Installation</span>



No installation required! Simply load the `nn.scm` file <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> your Scheme interpreter.



<span class="hljs-comment">### Requirements</span>

\- GNU Guile 3.0+ (recommended and tested)

\- For other implementations, see the Compatibility Notes section below



<span class="hljs-comment">### Compatibility</span>



This implementation is designed to work with:

\- \*\*GNU Guile\*\* (recommended): `guile -l nn.scm`

\- \*\*MIT Scheme\*\*: `scheme --load nn.scm`

\- \*\*Racket\*\*: `racket -f nn.scm` (may need minor adjustments <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> `#lang racket`)

\- \*\*Chicken Scheme\*\*: Load with `csi -s nn.scm`

class="ToolCodeBlock-module\_\_codeContainer\_\_YJrZ9"><pre class="ToolCodeBlock-module\_\_code\_\_X8Whj"><code class="ToolCodeBlock-module\_\_codeWrap\_\_HyFh6">$ <span class="hljs-built\_in">head</span> -50 /home/runner/work/nn.nn/nn.nn/lang/pli/snp.pli; <span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"===NEUROEVOLUTION==="</span>; <span class="hljs-built\_in">head</span> -40 /home/runner/work/nn.nn/nn.nn/lang/pli/neuroevolution.pli

/\*

&#x20;\* Spiking Neural P Systems (SN P) <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> PLingua

&#x20;\* The canonical membrane-computing formalism <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> neural networks

&#x20;\* (Ionescu, Paun, Yokomori 2006). This module bridges the nn.nn PLingua

&#x20;\* library to <span class="hljs-literal">true</span> SN P semantics:

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\*   - Neurons are membranes containing spike objects <span class="hljs-string">'a'</span>

&#x20;\*   - Firing rules: E / a^c -\&gt; a; d  (regular expression E over spikes,

&#x20;\*     consume c spikes, emit one spike after delay d)

&#x20;\*   - Forgetting rules: a^s -\&gt; lambda (remove spikes without firing)

&#x20;\*   - Synapses route emitted spikes to connected neurons

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Spike counts are natural numbers (object multiplicities); no x100

&#x20;\* scaling is needed - this is exact membrane computing.

&#x20;\*/



@model\&lt;spiking\_psystems\&gt;



/\* ============================================================================

&#x20;\* SN P NEURON

&#x20;\* A single spiking neuron with configurable firing threshold and delay.

&#x20;\* ============================================================================ \*/



@module snp\_neuron(threshold, delay)

{

&#x20;   @initial

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[neuron

&#x20;           spike\_count{0}

&#x20;           refractory{0}    /\* \&gt; 0 means neuron is closed (firing delay) \*/

&#x20;       ]<span class="hljs-string">'main

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Receive spikes (only when neuron is open) \*/

&#x20;   @rules receive

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       (a, in) \[spike\_count{s}, refractory{0}]'</span>neuron -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[spike\_count{s+1}, refractory{0}]<span class="hljs-string">'neuron

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Firing rule: a^threshold / a^threshold -\&gt; a; delay

&#x20;    \* When exactly enough spikes accumulate, consume them and

&#x20;    \* schedule a spike emission after '</span>delay<span class="hljs-string">' steps \*/

&#x20;   @rules fire

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[spike\_count{s}, refractory{0}]'</span>neuron -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[spike\_count{s - threshold}, refractory{delay},

&#x20;            pending\_spike{}]<span class="hljs-string">'neuron where s \&gt;= threshold

&#x20;   }



===NEUROEVOLUTION===

/\*

&#x20;\* Neuroevolution via Membrane Division Rules in PLingua

&#x20;\* Evolutionary training of neural networks using the native

&#x20;\* P-Systems operations:

&#x20;\*   - membrane DIVISION  = reproduction (a fit genome membrane

&#x20;\*     divides into an elite copy and a mutated offspring)

&#x20;\*   - membrane DISSOLUTION = selection death (unfit genomes dissolve)

&#x20;\*   - probabilistic evolution rules = mutation

&#x20;\*   - antiport communication = crossover between sibling genomes

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Each candidate network is a genome membrane whose gene{k, v}

&#x20;\* multiset encodes its weights; NEAT-flavored structural mutations

&#x20;\* add/remove edge objects and neuron membranes, tying neuroevolution

&#x20;\* to the gnn.pli edge representation for topology evolution.

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Uses the divide/dissolve macros sketched in integration.pli

&#x20;\* (plingua\_compat) and the random-guard probability convention from

&#x20;\* dropout.pli. Numerical convention: values scaled by 100.

&#x20;\*/



@model\&lt;membrane\_computing\&gt;



/\* ============================================================================

&#x20;\* GENOME MEMBRANE

&#x20;\* A candidate network: gene{k, v} objects (flattened weights) plus a

&#x20;\* fitness{f} object. Encode/decode rules map between a network'</span>s

&#x20;\* weight objects and the gene multiset.

&#x20;\* ============================================================================ \*/



@module genome\_membrane(genome\_size)

{

&#x20;   @initial

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[genome{1}

&#x20;           <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> (k = 1; k \&lt;= genome\_size; k++)

&#x20;           {

&#x20;               gene{k, random(-100, 100)}

&#x20;           }

&#x20;           fitness{0}

&#x20;       ]<span class="hljs-string">'main

=== nd purpose ===

%% nn\_nd.pl - Rank-parametric nD and fractal-dimensional extension of nn.pl

%%

%% Dimension is a parameter, not a class: the single `convnd` abstraction

%% replaces the TemporalConvolution / SpatialConvolution / VolumetricConvolution

%% triplet.  Everything reduces to three rank-generic primitives:

%%

%%   1. Strided index arithmetic  - map nD coordinates to flat offsets

%%   2. im2col / unfold (nD)      - lower convolution to matrix multiply

%%   3. Reduction over axis sets  - pooling / normalization / mean / max

%%

%% Output shape law (all ranks):

%%   out\_i = floor((in\_i + <span class="hljs-number">2</span>\*p\_i - d\_i\*(k\_i - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>) - <span class="hljs-number">1</span>) / s\_i) + <span class="hljs-number">1</span>,  i in <span class="hljs-number">1</span>..Rank

%%

%% Fractal dimensionality is supported in both readings:

%%   (a) fractal topology  - FractalNet-style self-similar container recursion

%%       (fractal\_module/<span class="hljs-number">3</span>, concat\_avg with drop-path regularization);

%%   (b) fractal data domains - non-integer Hausdorff dimension, handled by

%%       lowering to a weighted graph (sierpinski\_graph/<span class="hljs-number">2</span>) and replacing grid

%%       convolution with message passing (graph\_conv\_module/<span class="hljs-number">3</span>).  Multi-scale

%%       pooling follows the fractal's self-similar coarsening maps

%%       (fractal\_pool/<span class="hljs-number">3</span>): the renormalization structure of the fractal \*is\*

%%       the pooling hierarchy.

%%

%% The unifying principle: one parametric mechanism, three lowering paths

%% (GEMM for low rank, separable/tensor factorization for high rank,

%% spectral/graph methods for fractal rank).



:- module(nn\_nd, \[

&#x20;   % Output shape law (single invariant, all ranks)

&#x20;   conv\_output\_shape/<span class="hljs-number">6</span>,



&#x20;   % Rank-parametric convolution

&#x20;   convnd\_module/<span class="hljs-number">5</span>,

&#x20;   convnd\_module/<span class="hljs-number">8</span>,

&#x20;   convnd\_forward/<span class="hljs-number">3</span>,



&#x20;   % Separable / factorized convolution (high-rank lowering path)

&#x20;   separable\_convnd\_module/<span class="hljs-number">4</span>,



&#x20;   % Rank-parametric pooling

\-- a9nn/AtomSpace.lua

\-- OpenCog-inspired hypergraph knowledge base.

\--

\-- Atoms are the fundamental units: Nodes (typed, named) and Links (typed,

\-- connecting other atoms).  Each atom carries a TruthValue (strength + count)

\-- and an AttentionValue (STI + LTI).

\--

\-- This implementation is a pure-Lua in-memory store; it does not require any

\-- external dependencies.



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> nn    = require(<span class="hljs-string">'a9nn.nn\_ns'</span>)

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> Class = nn.Class



\-- ─── TruthValue ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> TruthValue = {}

TruthValue.\_\_index = TruthValue



<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> TruthValue.new(strength, count)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> setmetatable({

&#x20;     strength = strength or 1.0,

&#x20;     count    = count    or 1.0,

&#x20;  }, TruthValue)

end



<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> TruthValue:confidence()

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> self.count / (self.count + 1.0)

end



<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> TruthValue:\_\_tostring()

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> string.format(<span class="hljs-string">"\&lt;s=%.3f, c=%.1f\&gt;"</span>, self.strength, self.count)

end



\-- ─── AttentionValue ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> AttentionValue = {}

AttentionValue.\_\_index = AttentionValue



<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> AttentionValue.new(sti, lti)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> setmetatable({sti = sti or 0, lti = lti or 0}, AttentionValue)

end



\-- ─── Atom ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> Atom = {}

Atom.\_\_index = Atom

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> \_atomID = 0



<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> Atom.new(atomType, name, outgoing, tv, av)

&#x20;  \_atomID = \_atomID + 1

=== EPISODIC ===

\-- a9nn/EpisodicMemory.lua

\-- Episodic memory store with importance-weighted retrieval.

\--

\-- Memories are stored as {state, action, reward, nextState, info} tuples

\-- (standard RL experience tuples) plus optional free-form metadata.

\-- Retrieval can be by recency, importance, or similarity.



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> nn     = require(<span class="hljs-string">'a9nn.nn\_ns'</span>)

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> Tensor = nn.Tensor

<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> Class  = nn.Class



<span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> EpisodicMemory, \_ = Class.class(<span class="hljs-string">'nn.EpisodicMemory'</span>)



\--- @param capacity   maximum number of memories (default 1000)

\--- @param prioritised  use priority-weighted sampling (default <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>)

<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> EpisodicMemory:\_\_init(capacity, prioritised)

&#x20;  self.capacity    = capacity or 1000

&#x20;  self.prioritised = (prioritised == nil) and <span class="hljs-literal">true</span> or prioritised

&#x20;  self.buffer      = {}       -- circular buffer of experience tables

&#x20;  self.priorities  = {}       -- parallel priority array

&#x20;  self.head        = 1        -- write pointer

&#x20;  self.count       = 0        -- current fill level

&#x20;  self.alpha       = 0.6      -- priority exponent

&#x20;  self.beta        = 0.4      -- importance-sampling exponent

Let me deliver the analysis.</p>

<hr>

<h2>Analysis: Unique Abilities \&amp; Extension Opportunities Across Implementations</h2>

<p><strong>Yes — several implementations offer genuinely unique capabilities with no analog in the others.</strong> Here's a breakdown by implementation, ranked by distinctiveness.</p>

<h3>🥇 Tier 1: Truly Unique Capabilities (no equivalent elsewhere)</h3>

<p><strong>1. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/pli</code> (PLingua / P-Systems) — most differentiated</strong>

The only port that isn't a conventional von Neumann program. Membrane computing gives it abilities the others structurally cannot replicate:</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>Massive parallelism as a semantic primitive</strong> — P-System evolution rules apply concurrently by definition, not via threads. Extension: model <em>distributed training</em> (data-parallel gradients as inter-membrane communication) where parallelism is formally analyzable, not just concurrent.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>Membrane division/dissolution</strong> — already exploited by <code node="\[object Object]">neuroevolution.pli</code> (reproduction = division, death = dissolution). Extension: <strong>dynamic architecture search</strong> where networks grow/prune neurons and layers mid-training via native membrane create/dissolve rules — a natural fit that imperative ports emulate awkwardly.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>SN P systems</strong> (<code node="\[object Object]">snp.pli</code>) — spiking neurons are <em>the canonical</em> membrane formalism, exact (integer spike counts, no float scaling). Extension: <strong>neuromorphic computing models</strong> and event-driven inference, the only port that can natively express spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP).</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>Probabilistic guards</strong> (<code node="\[object Object]">prob\_rule</code> macro). Extension: stochastic regularization, Bayesian sampling as native probabilistic rule application.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>2. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/isa</code> (Isabelle/HOL) — machine-checked correctness</strong>

The only port where invariants are <em>proofs</em>, not tests (37 lemmas in <code node="\[object Object]">NN\_Properties.thy</code> alone): exact-real activations, <code node="\[object Object]">has\_real\_derivative</code> correctness of the derivatives used in training, softmax sums-to-one.</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">Extension: <strong>certified training</strong> — prove convergence bounds (e.g., gradient descent decreases loss for sufficiently small learning rates), verify backprop against the analytic derivative once, then <em>extract</em> verified code to OCaml/Scala/Haskell via Isabelle's code generator. This yields a proven-correct NN core no test suite can match. Also: prove numerical-stability properties of the <code node="\[object Object]">NN\_Exec</code> rational layer.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>3. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/a9nn</code> (Lua cognitive agents) — beyond NN into AGI-flavored systems</strong>

Unique modules: <code node="\[object Object]">AtomSpace</code> (OpenCog hypergraph with truth/attention values), <code node="\[object Object]">EpisodicMemory</code> (prioritized replay), <code node="\[object Object]">Personality</code>, <code node="\[object Object]">EchoReservoir</code> (ESN), <code node="\[object Object]">LLaMAOrchestrator</code> (parallel local LLM inference), <code node="\[object Object]">NNECCOAgent</code>.</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">Extension: <strong>neuro-symbolic fusion</strong> — link AtomSpace nodes to trained module weights so symbolic queries retrieve and <em>execute</em> subnetworks; reservoir–LLM hybridization where the ESN gates/routes prompts to the LLaMA pool; RL from AtomSpace attention values as intrinsic reward. This is the only port positioned to bridge deep learning and cognitive architectures.</li>

</ul>

<h3>🥈 Tier 2: Strong Unique Angles</h3>

<p><strong>4. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/pl</code> (Prolog) — logic-native NN</strong>

Two assets: relational/bidirectional semantics (predicates can run "backwards" — query which inputs produce a target output, i.e., <strong>network inversion for free</strong>) and <code node="\[object Object]">nn\_nd.pl</code>'s <strong>rank-parametric convolution</strong> — one <code node="\[object Object]">convnd</code> replaces the Temporal/Spatial/Volumetric triplet, with a <em>fractal-dimension</em> reading (graph-lowered conv on Sierpinski topologies).</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">Extension: <strong>differentiable logic programming / neural-symbolic ILP</strong> (DeepProbLog-style); use backtracking for architecture search; use unification for weight-tying and equivariance constraints; extend the fractal/graph path into a general GNN that the pli GNN currently leads.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>5. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/raku</code> — the only OO/gradual-typed port</strong>

Uses <code node="\[object Object]">role Module</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">class ... does Module</code> — the most idiomatic type system of the dynamic ports.</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">Extension: Raku's <code node="\[object Object]">race</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">hyper</code> for <strong>declarative data parallelism</strong> over batches; <code node="\[object Object]">grammar</code>s to parse/serialize network configs or ONNX-like formats; <code node="\[object Object]">subset</code> types for runtime shape validation (a poor-man's type-safe tensor API).</li>

</ul>

<h3>🥉 Tier 3: Reference/Pedagogical (extend for ecosystem, not capability)</h3>

<p><strong>6. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/scm</code> + <code node="\[object Object]">lang/rkt</code></strong> — nearly identical pure-functional cores. Racket's distinct angle: <code node="\[object Object]">#lang</code> language-oriented programming (a <strong>NN DSL</strong> with static shape checking at macro-expansion), and its maturity for teaching. Scheme's: minimalism/portability across Guile/MIT/Chicken.</p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">Extension (rkt): a <code node="\[object Object]">nn-lang</code> with compile-time shape inference and <code node="\[object Object]">contracts</code> for module I/O — the strongest fit for type-safe-by-construction nets.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>7. <code node="\[object Object]">lang/c</code> (THNN) + <code node="\[object Object]">lang/lua</code></strong> — the legacy Torch7 backend/reference. Not candidates for novel capability; their value is performance and historical parity. Only extend if native-kernel performance or Torch compatibility is the goal.</p>

<hr>

<h3>Recommended exploration (highest leverage first)</h3>

<table><thead><tr><th>Priority</th><th>Port</th><th>Extension</th><th>Why unique</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">pli</code></td><td>Native dynamic architecture search via membrane division</td><td>Semantically impossible elsewhere</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">isa</code></td><td>Prove SGD convergence; code-extract a verified kernel</td><td>Only correctness-by-construction port</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">pl</code></td><td>Network inversion via backtracking; neural-symbolic ILP</td><td>Bidirectional relational semantics</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">a9nn</code></td><td>AtomSpace↔weights neuro-symbolic execution</td><td>Only cognitive-architecture port</td></tr><tr><td>5</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">pli</code></td><td>STDP spiking networks on SN P systems</td><td>Canonical formalism, exact semantics</td></tr><tr><td>6</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">rkt</code></td><td><code node="\[object Object]">#lang nn</code> DSL with compile-time shape contracts</td><td>Language-oriented programming</td></tr><tr><td>7</td><td><code node="\[object Object]">raku</code></td><td><code node="\[object Object]">hyper</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">race</code> batch parallelism + <code node="\[object Object]">subset</code> shape types</td><td>Only gradual-typed OO port</td></tr></tbody></table>

<p><strong>Cross-cutting note:</strong> the shared <code node="\[object Object]">xor\_fixture.json</code> consistency harness means any new forward/loss semantics added to one port should be propagated to all seven — so the highest-leverage extensions are those that stay <em>within</em> one port's paradigm (Isabelle proofs, P-System dynamics, Prolog inversion) rather than new numerics that must be mirrored everywhere.</p>

/\*

&#x20;\* PLingua Integration Module

&#x20;\* Connects the P-Systems neural network implementation with existing

&#x20;\* PLingua tools, simulators, and standard P-Systems infrastructure.

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Provides:

&#x20;\*   1. Standard PLingua rule-set annotations compatible with pLinguaCore

&#x20;\*   2. Interface adaptors <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> external data ingestion

&#x20;\*   3. Export bridges (CSV, JSON, DOT, PNML)

&#x20;\*   4. Interoperability with Membrane Designer tools

&#x20;\*   5. Multi-membrane simulation harness

&#x20;\*   6. Standard P-Systems <span class="hljs-built\_in">type</span> system helpers

&#x20;\*   7. Benchmark suite and performance profiler

&#x20;\*   8. Module registry and dependency resolver

&#x20;\*/



@model\&lt;membrane\_computing\&gt;



/\* ============================================================================

&#x20;\* MODULE REGISTRY

&#x20;\* Tracks <span class="hljs-built\_in">which</span> modules are loaded, their versions, and dependencies.

&#x20;\* ============================================================================ \*/



@module module\_registry

{

&#x20;   @initial

&#x20;           module{batch\_normalization,   <span class="hljs-string">"1.0.0"</span>, \[nn]}

&#x20;           module{dropout,               <span class="hljs-string">"1.0.0"</span>, \[nn]}

&#x20;           /\* v2.1 extension modules \*/

<span class="hljs-comment">#!/usr/bin/env bash</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># validate.sh - Validation harness for the PLingua neural network sources.</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Usage:</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   ./validate.sh                 # structural checks only (no dependencies)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   PLINGUA=plingua ./validate.sh # additionally compile each file with the</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#                                 # P-Lingua 5 compiler (github.com/RGNC/plingua)</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>

<span class="hljs-comment"># Structural checks performed on every .pli file:</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   - balanced /\* ... \*/ comments</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   - balanced braces { }</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   - balanced brackets \[ ]</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#   - balanced parentheses ( )</span>

<span class="hljs-comment">#</span>

<span class="hljs-built\_in">set</span> -u



<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-subst">$(dirname <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$0</span>"</span>)</span>"</span>



fail=0

files=(\*.pli)



<span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"Validating <span class="hljs-variable">${#files\[@]}</span> PLingua source files..."</span>

<span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span>



<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> f <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">${files\[@]}</span>"</span>; <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;   errors=<span class="hljs-string">""</span>



&#x20;   <span class="hljs-comment"># Strip string literals, then check comment balance</span>

&#x20;   opens=$(grep -o <span class="hljs-string">'/\\\*'</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">wc</span> -l)

&#x20;   closes=$(grep -o <span class="hljs-string">'\\\*/'</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">wc</span> -l)

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> \[ <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$opens</span>"</span> -ne <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$closes</span>"</span> ]; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;       errors=<span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$errors</span> unbalanced-comments(<span class="hljs-variable">$opens</span>/<span class="hljs-variable">$closes</span>)"</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>



&#x20;   <span class="hljs-comment"># Remove comments and string literals before delimiter counting</span>

&#x20;   stripped=$(sed -e <span class="hljs-string">'s://.\*$::'</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>"</span> | awk <span class="hljs-string">'BEGIN{RS="\\0"} {gsub(/\\/\\\*\[^\*]\*\\\*+(\[^\\/\*]\[^\*]\*\\\*+)\*\\//, ""); gsub(/"\[^"]\*"/, ""); print}'</span>)



&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> pair <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> <span class="hljs-string">'{ }'</span> <span class="hljs-string">'\[ ]'</span> <span class="hljs-string">'( )'</span>; <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;       open\_ch=<span class="hljs-variable">${pair% \*}</span>

&#x20;       close\_ch=<span class="hljs-variable">${pair#\* }</span>

&#x20;       o=$(<span class="hljs-built\_in">printf</span> <span class="hljs-string">'%s'</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$stripped</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">tr</span> -<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$open\_ch</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">wc</span> -c)

&#x20;       c=$(<span class="hljs-built\_in">printf</span> <span class="hljs-string">'%s'</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$stripped</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">tr</span> -<span class="hljs-built\_in">cd</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$close\_ch</span>"</span> | <span class="hljs-built\_in">wc</span> -c)

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> \[ <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$o</span>"</span> -ne <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$c</span>"</span> ]; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;           errors=<span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$errors</span> unbalanced-$open\_ch<span class="hljs-variable">$close\_ch</span>(<span class="hljs-variable">$o</span>/<span class="hljs-variable">$c</span>)"</span>

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">done</span>



&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> \[ -n <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$errors</span>"</span> ]; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"FAIL  <span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>:<span class="hljs-variable">$errors</span>"</span>

&#x20;       fail=1

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">else</span>

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"ok    <span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>"</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>



&#x20;   <span class="hljs-comment"># Optional: full syntax check with the P-Lingua compiler</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> \[ -n <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">${PLINGUA:-}</span>"</span> ]; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> ! <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$PLINGUA</span>"</span> <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>"</span> \&gt; /dev/null 2\&gt;\&amp;1; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;           <span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"FAIL  <span class="hljs-variable">$f</span>: P-Lingua compiler rejected the file"</span>

&#x20;           fail=1

&#x20;       <span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>

<span class="hljs-keyword">done</span>



<span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span>

<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> \[ <span class="hljs-string">"<span class="hljs-variable">$fail</span>"</span> -ne 0 ]; <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"Validation FAILED"</span>

&#x20;   <span class="hljs-built\_in">exit</span> 1

<span class="hljs-keyword">fi</span>

<span class="hljs-built\_in">echo</span> <span class="hljs-string">"All files passed validation"</span>

Here's my analysis and plan.</p>

<hr>

<h2>P-Lingua Deep Dive + Hybrid Variant Assessment</h2>

<h3>First, answering your hybrid question directly</h3>

<p>Yes — all three hybrid ideas are worth exploring, and they each map cleanly onto what already exists in this repo. Here's my honest assessment of each:</p>

<p><strong>A. P-Lingua AtomSpace (<code node="\[object Object]">atomspace.pli</code>) — HIGH value, natural fit ⭐ recommended first</strong></p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">OpenCog's AtomSpace is a <em>hypergraph of typed atoms with truth/attention values</em>. This is almost isomorphic to P-Systems: atoms = objects, links = membranes containing their endpoints, <strong>attention spreading = rule-based multiset rewriting</strong>, ECAN (Economic Attention Network) = resource-competition rules competing for STI currency.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">We already have <code node="\[object Object]">a9nn/AtomSpace.lua</code> (TruthValue, AttentionValue, attention spreading) as a semantic reference to port, and <code node="\[object Object]">gnn.pli</code> already does message-passing over membranes-as-nodes — that's 80% of attention spreading.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">This is the <strong>strongest</strong> hybrid: it gives the pli port symbolic reasoning the other ports lack, and it's genuinely <em>more</em> natural in membrane computing than in Lua.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>B. <code node="\[object Object]">a9nn.pli</code> (NNECCO cognitive agent in P-Systems) — HIGH value, builds on A</strong></p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">The NNECCO agent (EchoReservoir, Personality, EpisodicMemory, 12-step EchoBeats, LLaMA orchestration) becomes tractable once AtomSpace exists. Reservoir = a membrane of recurrently-connected neurons; EchoBeats phases = rule phases; LLaMA pool = a population of membranes with load-balancing antiport rules.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Should come <strong>after</strong> atomspace.pli, reusing it.</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>C. P-Limbo (P-Systems on Inferno/Dis VM distributed grid) — INTRIGUING but speculative ⚠️</strong></p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]">This is the most novel but least grounded: Inferno's Limbo/Dis is a real distributed VM, and "membranes as Dis processes communicating over channels (Styx/9P)" is a <em>beautiful</em> conceptual match — membrane communication rules literally map to channel message-passing, and membrane tree = process tree.</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>But</strong> it's a different language/runtime, not PLingua, so it wouldn't live in <code node="\[object Object]">lang/pli</code> or pass <code node="\[object Object]">validate.sh</code>. It'd be a new <code node="\[object Object]">lang/limbo</code> port. Recommend scoping it as a <strong>design doc + minimal prototype</strong> rather than a full port, since Inferno tooling is niche and CI would be hard.</li>

</ul>

<h3>Recommended sequence</h3>

<ol>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">atomspace.pli</code> (foundation)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">a9nn.pli</code> (NNECCO agent on top of it)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">P-Limbo as exploratory design doc (separate, later)</li>

</ol>

<hr>

<h3>Proposed Plan: Phase 1 = <code node="\[object Object]">atomspace.pli</code></h3>

<p><strong>Goal:</strong> A P-Systems hypergraph knowledge base with truth values, attention values, and ECAN-style attention spreading — mirroring <code node="\[object Object]">a9nn/AtomSpace.lua</code> semantics in native membrane computing.</p>

<p><strong>New files (in <code node="\[object Object]">lang/pli/</code>):</strong></p>

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">atomspace.pli</code> — core module:

<ul>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">@model\&lt;membrane\_computing\&gt;</code></li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">@module atom\_node(type, name)</code> — ConceptNode/PredicateNode as membranes holding <code node="\[object Object]">tv{s,c}</code> (strength×count) and <code node="\[object Object]">av{sti,lti}</code> objects</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><code node="\[object Object]">@module atom\_link(type, ...)</code> — InheritanceLink/EvaluationLink as membranes <em>containing</em> their endpoint atoms (true hypergraph nesting)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Truth-value revision rules (merge duplicate atoms: combine strength/confidence)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]"><strong>ECAN attention spreading</strong>: antiport rules diffusing STI along links, source atoms paying "wages", receiving atoms collecting "income" — resource-competition is native to P-Systems</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Hebbian learning: co-activated atoms form/strengthen links</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Pattern matcher: query by type/name via membrane queries</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Attentional focus = the membrane region where STI \&gt; threshold</li>

</ul>

</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Tests: append \~8 atomspace tests to <code node="\[object Object]">test\_extensions.pli</code> (node/link creation, TV revision, STI diffusion convergence, Hebbian link formation, pattern match, attentional-focus selection)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Demos: append 1–2 demos to <code node="\[object Object]">demo.pli</code> (build a small knowledge graph, run ECAN, show attentional focus)</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Register in <code node="\[object Object]">integration.pli</code> <code node="\[object Object]">module\_registry</code> (<code node="\[object Object]">module{atomspace, "1.0.0", \[nn]}</code>) + re-export rules</li>

<li node="\[object Object]">Update <code node="\[object Object]">lang/pli/README.md</code> with a new section</li>

</ul>

<p><strong>Validation:</strong> <code node="\[object Object]">bash lang/pli/validate.sh</code> (all balanced-delimiter + comment checks must pass), plus <code node="\[object Object]">luacheck</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">mkdocs</code> untouched. No change to the shared XOR fixture (atomspace adds no float forward/loss semantics), so cross-port consistency is preserved.</p>

<p><strong>Conventions I'll follow</strong> (verified against existing code): values scaled ×100 as integers, <code node="\[object Object]">@module</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">@rules</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">@initial</code> structure, <code node="\[object Object]">where</code> guards, the <code node="\[object Object]">prob\_rule</code>/divide/dissolve macros from <code node="\[object Object]">integration.pli</code>, and the <code node="\[object Object]">@test</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">@description</code>/<code node="\[object Object]">@setup</code> test idiom from <code node="\[object Object]">test\_nn.pli</code>.</p>

<hr>

<p>Shall I proceed with <strong>Phase 1 (<code node="\[object Object]">atomspace.pli</code>)</strong> as scoped above? Or would you prefer I also fold in a minimal <strong><code node="\[object Object]">a9nn.pli</code> skeleton</strong> (NNECCO agent membrane) in the same pass, or write the <strong>P-Limbo design doc</strong> first? My recommendation is atomspace first — it's the foundation both other ideas build on — but happy to adjust the batch. 🙂</p></div></div><div class="SessionFooter-module\_\_footer\_\_uEbNi end



\--- Add or retrieve a Node.

\-- @param atomType  string, e.g. <span class="hljs-string">"ConceptNode"</span>

\-- @param name      string identifier

\-- @param tv        TruthValue (optional)

\-- @<span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span>          Atom

<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> AtomSpace:addNode(atomType, name, tv)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> key = atomType .. <span class="hljs-string">"|"</span> .. name

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> self.nodeIndex\[key] <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> existing = self.atoms\[self.nodeIndex\[key]]

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> tv <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> existing.tv = tv end

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> existing

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> atom = Atom.new(atomType, name, {}, tv)

&#x20;  self.atoms\[atom.id]    = atom

&#x20;  self.nodeIndex\[key]    = atom.id

&#x20;  self.typeIndex\[atomType] = self.typeIndex\[atomType] or {}

&#x20;  table.insert(self.typeIndex\[atomType], atom.id)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> atom

end



\--- Add or retrieve a Link.

\-- @param atomType  string, e.g. <span class="hljs-string">"InheritanceLink"</span>

\-- @param outgoing  list of Atom objects (or IDs)

\-- @param tv        TruthValue (optional)

\-- @<span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span>          Atom

<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> AtomSpace:addLink(atomType, outgoing, tv)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> ids = {}

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> \_, a <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> ipairs(outgoing) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;     ids\[#ids+1] = <span class="hljs-built\_in">type</span>(a) == <span class="hljs-string">"table"</span> and a.id or a

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> key = atomType .. <span class="hljs-string">"|"</span> .. table.concat(ids, <span class="hljs-string">","</span>)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> self.linkIndex\[key] <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> existing = self.atoms\[self.linkIndex\[key]]

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> tv <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> existing.tv = tv end

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> existing

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> atom = Atom.new(atomType, <span class="hljs-string">""</span>, ids, tv)

&#x20;  self.atoms\[atom.id]   = atom

&#x20;  self.linkIndex\[key]   = atom.id

&#x20;  self.typeIndex\[atomType] = self.typeIndex\[atomType] or {}

&#x20;  table.insert(self.typeIndex\[atomType], atom.id)

&#x20;  -- Update incoming sets

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> \_, <span class="hljs-built\_in">id</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> ipairs(ids) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> self.atoms\[<span class="hljs-built\_in">id</span>] <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;        self.atoms\[<span class="hljs-built\_in">id</span>].incoming\[atom.id] = <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>

&#x20;     end

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> atom

end

\--- Incoming <span class="hljs-built\_in">set</span> of an atom (links that reference it).

\--- Simple pattern matching: <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> links of given <span class="hljs-built\_in">type</span> whose outgoing <span class="hljs-built\_in">set</span>

\--- contains all of the supplied atoms (<span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> any position).

<span class="hljs-keyword">function</span> AtomSpace:getLinks(linkType, atoms)

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> mustHave = {}

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> \_, a <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> ipairs(atoms or {}) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;     mustHave\[<span class="hljs-built\_in">type</span>(a)==<span class="hljs-string">"table"</span> and a.id or a] = <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> results = {}

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> \_, atom <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> pairs(self.atoms) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;     <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> atom.type == linkType and atom:isLink() <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span>

&#x20;        <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> match = <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>

&#x20;        <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> <span class="hljs-built\_in">id</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> pairs(mustHave) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;           <span class="hljs-built\_in">local</span> found = <span class="hljs-literal">false</span>

&#x20;           <span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> \_, oid <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> ipairs(atom.outgoing) <span class="hljs-keyword">do</span>

&#x20;              <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> oid == <span class="hljs-built\_in">id</span> <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> found = <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>; <span class="hljs-built\_in">break</span> end

&#x20;           end

&#x20;           <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> not found <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> match = <span class="hljs-literal">false</span>; <span class="hljs-built\_in">break</span> end

&#x20;        end

&#x20;        <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> match <span class="hljs-keyword">then</span> results\[#results+1] = atom end

&#x20;     end

&#x20;  end

&#x20;  <span class="hljs-built\_in">return</span> results

end

@module plingua\_compat

{

&#x20;   /\* Standard evolution rule wrapper \*/

&#x20;   @macro evolution\_rule(lhs, rhs, membrane)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[lhs]<span class="hljs-string">'membrane -\&gt; \[rhs]'</span>membrane

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Symport rule: move objects across membrane boundary \*/

&#x20;   @macro symport\_in(objects, membrane)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       (objects, <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span>) -\&gt; \[objects]<span class="hljs-string">'membrane

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @macro symport\_out(objects, membrane)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[objects]'</span>membrane -\&gt; (objects, out)

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Antiport rule: exchange objects across membrane boundary \*/

&#x20;   @macro antiport(objects\_in, objects\_out, membrane)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[objects\_out]<span class="hljs-string">'membrane (objects\_in, in) -\&gt;

&#x20;       \[objects\_in]'</span>membrane (objects\_out, out)

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Dissolution rule: dissolve membrane, objects go to parent \*/

&#x20;   @macro dissolve(membrane, objects)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[objects]<span class="hljs-string">'membrane -\&gt; objects     /\* membrane dissolved \*/

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Division rule: one membrane becomes two \*/

&#x20;   @macro divide(membrane, left\_objects, right\_objects)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[membrane] -\&gt; \[left\_objects]'</span>new\_left \[right\_objects]<span class="hljs-string">'new\_right

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Probabilistic rule: fire lhs -\&gt; rhs with probability p (0-100).

&#x20;    \* Maps onto native probabilistic P-System rules where supported;

&#x20;    \* otherwise uses the random-guard convention (see bayesian.pli). \*/

&#x20;   @macro prob\_rule(p, lhs, rhs, membrane)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[lhs]'</span>membrane -\&gt; \[rhs]<span class="hljs-string">'membrane where random(0, 100) \&lt; p

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   /\* Priority annotation \*/

&#x20;   @macro high\_priority(rule)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       @priority(1) rule

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @macro low\_priority(rule)

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       @priority(99) rule

&#x20;   }

}

/\*

&#x20;\* Graph Neural Network Modules <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> PLingua

&#x20;\* Membranes as graph nodes: each graph node is a membrane \[node{i} ...]

&#x20;\* holding feature objects feat{d, v}; edges are edge{i, j, w} objects

&#x20;\* <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> the enclosing graph membrane, so the membrane structure itself is

&#x20;\* the graph and message passing maps onto inter-membrane communication.

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Modules:

&#x20;\*   - message\_passing: send/aggregate neighbor features (<span class="hljs-built\_in">sum</span>/mean/max)

&#x20;\*   - gcn\_layer:       degree-normalized graph convolution + backward

&#x20;\*   - graph\_attention\_layer: GAT-style per-edge attention coefficients

&#x20;\*   - graph\_readout:   global <span class="hljs-built\_in">sum</span>/mean/max pooling to a graph embedding

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Degree normalization: node degrees deg{i} are precomputed <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> @initial

&#x20;\* (or accumulated from edge objects); aggregated features are divided

&#x20;\* by deg to give the symmetric-normalization approximation used by GCN.

&#x20;\* Self-loops: edge{i, i, 100} objects (weight 1.0) are added <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span>

&#x20;\* @initial so every node includes its own features <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> the aggregate.

&#x20;\*

&#x20;\* Numerical convention: values scaled by 100, consistent with nn.pli.

&#x20;\*/



@model\&lt;membrane\_computing\&gt;



/\* ============================================================================

&#x20;\* MESSAGE PASSING

&#x20;\* For each edge (i -\&gt; j), copy the <span class="hljs-built\_in">source</span> node<span class="hljs-string">'s features into the

&#x20;\* target node as msg{j, d, v} objects, then reduce incoming messages

&#x20;\* per node with the pairwise-reduction idiom from attention.pli.

&#x20;\* ============================================================================ \*/



@module message\_passing(num\_nodes, feat\_dim)

{

&#x20;   @initial

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[graph

&#x20;           for (i = 1; i \&lt;= num\_nodes; i++)

&#x20;           {

&#x20;               \[node{i}]'</span>graph

&#x20;               /\* Self-loop so a node sees its own features \*/

&#x20;               edge{i, i, 100}

&#x20;           }

&#x20;       ]<span class="hljs-string">'main

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @rules send\_messages

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       /\* Node i exposes its features to the graph membrane \*/

&#x20;       \[feat{d, v}]'</span>node{i} -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[feat{d, v}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{i} (node\_feat{i, d, v}, out)



&#x20;       /\* Each edge routes a weighted copy to the target node \*/

&#x20;       \[node\_feat{i, d, v}, edge{i, j, w}]'</span>graph -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[node\_feat{i, d, v}, edge{i, j, w},

&#x20;            msg{j, d, round(v\*w/100)}]<span class="hljs-string">'graph



&#x20;       /\* Deliver messages into the target node membrane \*/

&#x20;       \[msg{j, d, v}]'</span>graph -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[msg{d, v}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{j}

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @rules aggregate\_sum

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       /\* Pairwise sum of incoming messages per dimension \*/

&#x20;       \[msg{d, v1}, msg{d, v2}]'</span>node{j} -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[msg{d, v1+v2}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{j}



&#x20;       \[msg{d, v}, agg\_done{d}]'</span>node{j} -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[agg{d, v}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{j}

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @rules aggregate\_mean

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       /\* Mean variant: divide the summed messages by the node degree \*/

&#x20;       \[agg{d, v}, deg{n}, use\_mean{}]'</span>node{j} -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[agg{d, round(v/n)}, deg{n}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{j}

&#x20;   }



&#x20;   @rules aggregate\_max

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       /\* Max variant: pairwise max instead of sum \*/

&#x20;       \[msg{d, v1}, msg{d, v2}, use\_max{}]'</span>node{j} -\&gt;

&#x20;           \[msg{d, max(v1, v2)}, use\_max{}]<span class="hljs-string">'node{j}

&#x20;   }

}



/\* ============================================================================

&#x20;\* GCN LAYER

&#x20;\* Graph convolution: aggregate neighbor features weighted by

&#x20;\* degree-normalized edge weights, then apply a shared linear

&#x20;\* projection and ReLU. Backward rules propagate gradients back

&#x20;\* along the (reversed) edges, in the simplified style of nn.pli.

&#x20;\* ============================================================================ \*/



@module gcn\_layer(num\_nodes, in\_dim, out\_dim)

{

&#x20;   @initial

&#x20;   {

&#x20;       \[gcn

&#x20;           /\* Shared projection weights across all nodes \*/

&#x20;           for (d1 = 1; d1 \&lt;= in\_dim; d1++)

&#x20;           {

&#x20;               for (d2 = 1; d2 \&lt;= out\_dim; d2++)

&#x20;               {

&#x20;                   weight{d1, d2, random(-50, 50)}

&#x20;               }

&#x20;           }

&#x20;           for (d2 = 1; d2 \&lt;= out\_dim; d2++)

&#x20;           {

&#x20;               bias{d2, 0}

&#x20;           }



&#x20;           for (i = 1; i \&lt;= num\_nodes; i++)

&#x20;           {

&#x20;               \[node{i}

&#x20;                   deg{1}      /\* self-loop counts once; incremented per edge \*/

&#x20;               ]'</span>gcn

&#x20;               edge{i, i, 100}

&#x20;           }

&#x20;       ]<span class="hljs-string">'main

</span></code></pre></div></figure></div></div></div></div><div class="Tool-module\_\_toolContainer\_\_PQCpK"><div class="ToolGroupRenderer-module\_\_toolGroupHeader\_\_zA5xT"><div @module bayes\_linear\_layer(input\_size, output\_size)

```plingua
